sentences.text: MR P P MAJMUDAR(5284) WITH MR TEJAS K MOTWANI for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MS. SHIVANGI M RANA(7053) for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MS MOXA K THAKKAR, ADDL.
PUBLIC PROSECUTOR(2) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1 RULE SERVED BY DS(65) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 2 ============================================

=
CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE G.R.UDHWANI  Date : 19/06/2018
ORAL ORDER 1.

Petitioner has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 2(9)(k) and 7(2)(5) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short PFA Act) and Rule 32(e) of the Food Adulteration Rules (for short Rules) and has been sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for 1 year with a fine of Rs.2,000/- in default of which additional sentence of simple imprisonment for 3 months has been imposed upon him by the judgment and order dated 03.07.2017 rendered in Criminal Appeal No.7 of 2005 by the learned 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Panchmahal, District Godhra.

entities.text: 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Panchmahal, District Godhra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said conviction was by confirmation of the judgment and order dated 10.01.2005 rendered by the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Kalol, in Criminal Case No.618 of 1996.
The petitioner was held guilty for misbranding of certain food articles.

R/CR.RA/660/2017 ORDER Bansilal Manilal Shah vs State Of Gujarat on 19 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63078048/
1 2.

The learned counsel for the petitioner has invited the attention of this Court to Nemi Chand Vs.
State of Rajasthan, Criminal Appeal No.214 of 2016 arising out of SLP (Criminal) No.2148 of 2013 decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.

entities.text:
Nemi Chand Vs.
State of Rajasthan, Criminal Appeal No.214 of 2016
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The learned counsel has further pointed out that by passing the further orders the order rendered in Nemi Chand (Supra) came to be clarified by order dated 17.03.2016, which reads as under:
"Upon being mentioned by Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned senior counsel for the appellant, the 8th line of page no.2 of order dated March 10, 2016, passed in the aforementioned criminal appeal, i.e., A "He has, in this behalf, argued that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Section 16A was added and under the said section, only a fine is leviable.

A is substituted by the following: A "He has, in this behalf, argued that under Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the maximum penalty is only fine for sub-standard food or misbranding.

A (Nidhi Ahuja)."
2.1
The learned counsel submitted that in Nemi Chand (Supra) Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety And Standards Act, 2006 were retrospectively applied even to the pending cases.
He submitted that in the instant case also except misbranding, no other charge was led against the petitioner, that the punishment for misbranding contemplated in Section 52 is fine only.

The learned counsel therefore,
urged to extend the benefit of the said provisions to the petitioner as well.
He would submit that the petitioner would not press for the petition on other merits of the case.
3. None of the opponents were able to contend contrary to what R/CR.RA/660/2017 ORDER the learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted.

In Nemi Chand (Supra) benefit of Section 51 of the Act of 2006 came to be extended by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case arising under old law i.e.
Act of 1954; the relevant observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court are thus:
"It is not in dispute that the charge against the appellant was only of sub-standardization of goods.

Mr. Sushil Kumar Jain, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that though the appellant has some prima facie case even on merits, he would be giving up the plea on merits and his only submission is about the sentence which has been imposed by the courts below.
He has, in this behalf, argued that there has been an amendment in the Act by the Central Amendment Act 34 of 1976 whereby Section 16A was added and under the said section, only a fine is leviable.

He has drawn our attention to the judgment of this Court in 'T. Barai v. Henry Ah Hoe and Another' [1983 (1) SCC 177] wherein this Court held that since the amendment was beneficial to the accused persons, it can be applied even with respect to earlier cases as well which are pending in the Court."
4.

entities.text: T. Barai v. Henry Ah Hoe and Another' [1983 (1) SCC 177]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As indicated above, the original order in Nemi Chand (Supra) came to be clarified by subsequent order quoted hereinabove and thus, clearly the provisions of Section 51 were applied to the cases arising under old law and pending in Appeal or other proceedings on the date of commencement of the Act of 2006.
The present case would fall under Section 52 of the Act of 2006, which provides a penalty extending to Rs.3 Lacs for dealing with misbranded food article.

Bansilal Manilal Shah vs State Of Gujarat on 19 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63078048/
2 5.

entities.text: Bansilal Manilal Shah vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In above view of the matter, the case for modification of the R/CR.RA/660/2017 ORDER sentence in the impugned judgment is made out.
In the facts and circumstances of the case, a fine of Rs.25,000/- would meet the ends of justice.

Accordingly, the impugned order of sentence is modified and instead of imprisonment, it is directed that the petitioner shall bear a fine of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) which shall be deposited within two weeks from today, failing which the sentence imposed by the court below shall stand revived without reference to this Court.
The petition is disposed of.
